Changelog

What’s new in BenchPilot

Every release of the Chrome extension, newest first. 22 releases since 30 September 2026.

Version 1.20.1 18 November 2026

The drawer shows your account and waiting synced data (17 Nov)

  • The ⋯ menu in the LinkedIn drawer starts with the account BenchPilot is signed in to ("Signed in as you@example.com", "with Google"), or "Not signed in", and an Account and sign out (or Sign in) item. The plan chip's tooltip points to it (your email is never in the tooltip).
  • When your encrypted sync needs you on this computer (locked, set up on a new computer, approve a computer, paused, a problem), a banner over every tab says so, with Open (Settings, Sync). Before, only the toolbar popup said it, so a new computer just looked empty.
  • Signing in or out on another BenchPilot page updates the drawer's plan chip and account row at once, not at the next reload of the LinkedIn tab.

Version 1.20.0 17 November 2026

Consultant portal for teams, and a page for independent consultants (17 Nov; spec docs/specs/CONSULTANT_PORTAL_SPEC.md)

  • The consultant link becomes the consultant's own page, paid for by the firm and free for the consultant. Besides availability, rate, location and consent, the consultant can update their work authorisation end date (the saved date is never shown). They see only the submissions the firm shares (role, end client, a plain status and the date; never vendors, rates or the recruiter), and can give or decline the RTR for each.
  • Duplicate protection from the consultant's side: the consultant can flag "another firm already submitted me here" on a shared submission, and list end clients other firms submitted them to in the last 90 days. The submission form then warns when you submit to one of them (the warning never blocks). Entries are deleted after 90 days, and erasing the consultant deletes them.
  • Web app: "Share with the consultant" on the new-submission form and in "RTR and rate"; a chip on flagged submissions (Clear); "What <name> told you" on the consultant's link card; a "Duplicate?" card at the top of the recruiter's Today's plan for each flagged submission.
  • Website: a new page for independent consultants ("Market yourself like a bench desk", Solo as it is). The privacy policy and terms are updated: firms must never charge consultants a fee, fabricate résumés, use proxy interviews, or act as an OPT employer of record.

Today's plan: your shift, planned and driven, with no AI (16 Nov; built as "Day Pilot", spec docs/specs/DAY_PILOT_SPEC.md)

  • "Today's homework" becomes Today's plan: one plan for the shift, in seven blocks that follow the US day (Start, Replies, Requirements, Submit, Wave 2 and hotlist, Follow-ups, Close) from your shift start.
  • One card at a time on the dashboard Today page and in the LinkedIn drawer: what it is, why it is next, and one-click answers ("Sent?", "Any reply? Replied / Interview / Rejected", "Still available?", "Sent the hotlist"), with Skip (with a reason), Later and Next. A Focus / List switch; N and S keys on the dashboard. The popup shows the next card.
  • New cards from data you already have: bench check, consent missing, reply check, RTR missing or ending, almost a match, hotlist due, target pace (Solo), vendor agreements, timesheets and invoices. Urgent cards (an interview within 90 minutes, a fresh 80 %+ match) come first.
  • A start-of-shift briefing (yesterday's numbers on Solo) and Close my day: what is left, what carries over, and the end-of-day report written from your day (Solo): copy it, download the CSV, or open it as an email to your manager. BenchPilot never sends it.
  • Today's plan learns from skips: a vendor you mark "doesn't reply" ranks lower for 14 days; a skipped match teaches the match ranking. Settings > Today's plan shows what it learned (Reset), your daily target and your manager's email.
  • Nothing new leaves your browser and the saved-data shape does not change (new optional settings only). The Today cards for vendor agreements and timesheets / invoices are now Today's plan cards.

Web app: sign-in page fix (16 Nov)

  • The sign-in page no longer shows the word "null" under "Continue with Google" while the Microsoft button is switched off. A test now stops the same mistake anywhere in the web app.

One look everywhere (owner, 16 Nov; reverses the white headers of 27 Oct)

  • The LinkedIn drawer, every extension page, the web app and the pictures on the website share one look: the purple header band with the logo, the plan chip and white icons, and the numbers as yellow figures on darker purple tiles.
  • Every page opens with the purple header band: popup, dashboard (the logo cell and the top bar), Today, Settings, Plans, Account, Welcome and Help. Logo tile, "BenchPilot" in white, the plan chip, and the numbers as tiles (yellow figures on the darker plate).
  • The same plan chip everywhere, with the drawer's words: "FREE · 2/3", "SOLO", yellow "FREE · 3/3 · UPGRADE" at the limit. The dashboard shows it in the top bar; the Plans page shows the plan word.
  • Fixes: a consultant's name no longer disappears behind its chips on Bench cards; Settings fields are white like every other field; no dark strip around Settings in the dark theme; the Plans page "Bring BenchPilot to your team" card has no blank strip under its button.
  • Text fields, lists and the search box show one purple focus ring when you click them; the dark ring is only for moving with the keyboard.

Encrypted sync across computers is on (Solo; Pro holders keep it)

  • Settings → Sync across computers: your data, and your résumé files, are encrypted in your browser; the server holds a copy it can't read. It turns itself on when you buy Solo (save the recovery code it shows); add a passphrase if you like; approve a new computer from one you already use. Free users can keep one encrypted backup in their account.

Run your staffing desk in BenchPilot (14 Nov; extension and web app)

  • Consultants: work authorisation as a type (H1B, GC, USC, OPT/CPT…) with its end date and reminders at 120/90/60/30/7 days; minimum rate; available-from date and bench status. Only the type and date are kept, never document copies.
  • Submissions: RTR with the date, end date and agreed rate (instead of a tick box); bill rate, pay rate and margin; the vendor → prime → client chain; Request RTR opens an email for you to send; soft warnings when a rate differs from the RTR or the RTR has ended. In a team, pay rates are visible to owners and managers unless the owner allows recruiters.
  • Interviews and placements: rounds with time zones and a calendar file (.ics); placements with start and end dates, rates, margin per hour and an estimate per month; a Placements view and a QuickBooks-friendly CSV.
  • Vendor agreements: MSA and NDA status and dates, net payment terms, reminders before they end, and a gentle "no MSA on file" note when you submit.
  • Consent and data requests: record a consultant's consent, a data-notice email draft, export or erase one consultant everywhere, and a typed call / WhatsApp / notes log.
  • Targets: personal targets and your funnel on Insights (Solo), also by skill family; team targets, a leaderboard and funnel reports in the web app.
  • Profile summary and consultant links: a one-page masked profile (no contact details) for hotlists and pitches; Google / Outlook calendar links next to the .ics; in a team, a private link where a consultant confirms availability and rate and gives RTR consent.

Simpler everywhere (UX decisions, 14 Nov)

  • The popup is a launcher: today's three numbers, one status line (with Pause), Open dashboard and Open drawer. The lead list, Copy/Export/Save bar, Times and Scan this page are gone (capture is automatic).
  • One Settings page, grouped: You · Matching · Look · Data · Account & plan.
  • Dashboard: one main button per page; Export in the ⋯ menu; "Copy N emails (for BCC)" when you select requirements; the time converter on Today; vendor Heat is now relative (the busiest vendors), so not every vendor shows Hot.
  • Sync turns itself on for paid plans (see the sync section above).

Timesheets, invoices and commission estimates (staffing "Later" F1, F2, G4; migrations 0055 and 0057, storage schema 21; plan and copy wait for Nick)

  • Timesheets: weekly regular and overtime hours per placement, who approved them (typed), Draft / Submitted / Approved. No files, no client logins. Weeks missing on a placement that uses timesheets show on Today (and as a count in the team's morning report).
  • Invoices (a tracker, not accounting): made from the approved weeks x the hourly bill rate, overtime at its own rate, due on the vendor's net terms (default Net 30). Draft / Sent / Paid with the payment day; Overdue = sent and past the due date (Today and the morning report, counts only). Print or save as PDF from the browser and "Email draft" in your own mail app: BenchPilot never sends an invoice. CSV for QuickBooks (MM/DD/YYYY), Zoho Books (YYYY-MM-DD) or Tally (DD-MM-YYYY). The firm's details print on the invoice.
  • Commission: a default rule and one per recruiter (% of the month's margin estimate or a fixed amount per placement, with an optional lead share), the estimate per person per month and a CSV. Labelled as estimates, not payroll. Owners and managers who may see pay.
  • "Export everything" (0057) includes the timesheets for every exporter, and the invoices and commission rules for owners and managers only. The extension's backup carries them on each submission, plus your invoice details and commission rule.
  • Team workspace (Team · 15 and 40, and the pilot): Timesheets for everyone; Invoices and Commission for owners and managers. Extension: recording weeks is free; invoices, print / PDF, the invoice CSV, your invoice details and your commission estimate are Solo.

Extension: capture is automatic (UX decisions P1; waiting for Nick's OK)

  • New installs save every recruiter you scroll past (on this computer only); the welcome tour says so once. The first-run "how should recruiters be saved?" question and its Today checklist step are gone (4 steps now).
  • Users who had autosave off are never switched over: the drawer offers it once ("Turn on" / "Keep picking"). The drawer's Settings sheet has the switch.
  • "Scanner" is now "Pause BenchPilot on LinkedIn" in the drawer ⋯ menu; while paused, a banner with Resume shows on every tab.
  • The drawer drops Save all, Copy emails, Export CSV and the per-recruiter Copy buttons (Draft email fills in the address). The toolbar badge and the dock show only new strong matches and follow-ups due, never the page's lead count.
  • Drawer polish: Requirements filters behind one "Filters" button with removable chips; "Good fits" is "Matches" everywhere; no bar at the bottom: Dashboard is an icon in the header, Quick notes and Keyboard shortcuts are in the More menu, and "?" opens the shortcut list; the focus ring follows the selected tab; the dock hides while the drawer is open; recruiter titles wrap instead of being cut; the recruiter type moved into the open card; Bench shows one count line and no disabled "Draft email" at 0 matches; the plan-sheet price uses the body font.

A new look (one BenchPilot, one plan ladder)

  • The popup is rebuilt as a launcher (see "Simpler everywhere"): plan chip, today's numbers, one status line, Open dashboard and Open drawer. No more overlapping plan line.
  • One plan sheet everywhere: a locked feature opens the same sheet (what Solo adds, the price, Upgrade to Solo, Not now). "Not now" quiets that prompt for 7 days.
  • The drawer header shows your plan (FREE · 2/3 consultants, SOLO); the dashboard sidebar has a plan card and Invite a teammate; Today has a "Get set up" checklist.
  • The Plans page shows the one ladder: Free, Solo and Team (5, 15 or 40 people, starting a 14-day team pilot in the web app).
  • Empty states, denser tables with sticky headers, and polish across the dashboard, Settings, Account and Welcome, in light and dark.

Buying and plan screens (A-to-Z audit, 14 Nov)

  • Solo can be bought from the extension. Choose Solo, Renew and Upgrade used to fail with "Please choose a valid plan" (the checkout only knew the retired Basic/Pro ids); a sign-up in the middle of a purchase now keeps the plan.
  • Lock badges and upsells say SOLO (no more "BASIC+" or "PRO"), and every paywall shows the price: "Solo ₹499/month or ₹3,999/year" ($12 / $99 outside India).
  • One rule for "your plan is ending": the popup, the drawer and the dashboard all warn in the last 14 days. After a paid plan ends, the drawer and the popup say "expired · Renew as Solo" for 7 days (also when you are signed in).
  • Moving from Basic or Pro to Solo says how your leftover days convert by price ("N days of Pro become M days of Solo"), instead of "kept".
  • The founding button turns off with "All 100 founding places are taken" when they are gone; founding members keep "Your founding price" for their 12 months. The "Most chosen" ribbon is gone.
  • The comparison and the Solo list now show everything Solo includes: the personal inbox address, My book on the web, the morning summary and vendor check-ins.
  • The account page has the 6-digit code box for verifying your email, shows the last payment again (₹ or $), formats the end date, links to the web app (Open my book), and links a team owner who tries to delete their account to the workspace settings.
  • Privacy policy and Terms links where you type your email (welcome and sign-up). Every line that said your data or résumé "never leaves this computer" now says what happens with Solo sync on.
  • Exports: a Heat column and a "Hottest vendors first" order. The Today day-start setting says it follows India time.
  • Bring BenchPilot to your team: the reward reads "90 days of Solo".
  • Your work terms (tax terms) now sync with your other settings.

Team: the Starter bench holds up to 25 consultants (final plan §8)

  • Import adds consultants up to the cap and reports the rest as "not added: the bench is full".

Copy: resume files and Solo sync (draft text for Nick's approval)

  • Since sync phase 2 (PR #311) Solo sync also syncs resume files, encrypted in the browser. The site FAQ, privacy policy (site and extension copy), Terms 7a and the store listing draft no longer say resume files are never synced: on Free they stay on the computer; on Solo with sync on they are encrypted and synced, the server cannot read them, and turning sync off deletes them from the server.

Delete my account (backlog E11; server deploy and the privacy-policy line wait for Nick)

  • Extension account page and web app (#account, linked from the top bar): "Delete my account" deletes your BenchPilot account yourself (until now only by writing to us). You confirm it is you (password or Google again in the extension; a 6-digit email code in the web app), type your email, then delete.
  • What goes: your sign-in, plan and plan grants, encrypted synced copy and resume files, personal inbox. What stays: payments (for tax records, no longer linked to you), a referral reward that was paid (anonymous), anonymous feedback. In a team you leave it and what you added stays with the team. A team owner is asked to transfer or delete the workspace first.
  • This computer: your data stays and keeps working without an account, unless you tick "Also clear BenchPilot data on this computer" (off by default; it offers a backup first and then starts like a new install).

Web app: My book v2 (backlog W9)

  • Add and delete recruiters, vendors, consultants, submissions, notes and jobs in My book. New records use the extension's own rules (duplicate checks, limits, the duplicate-submission guard); a deletion syncs to every computer like one made in the extension.
  • More edits: vendors (name, label, notes), submissions (status, follow-up, rate asked, RTR note), notes and email templates.
  • Morning summary is the first page of My book: yesterday's requirements saved, submissions sent, vendor replies and interviews, counted in your browser from your encrypted book, the same way as Today in the extension.
  • Resume files: see the resume files synced from the extension and download one; it is decrypted in your browser tab.
  • Changed on two computers: if you and another computer change the same field within a minute, pick which version to keep. Change passphrase from the web app (Replace my keys stays in the extension).

Inboxes: where a requirement came from, and per-job Ignore that sticks (#308 follow-ups)

  • Requirements show where they came from: a requirement added from a team-inbox email is Team inbox; one added from a job-board alert shows the board by name (Dice, Indeed, LinkedIn Job Alerts, ZipRecruiter, Monster, CareerBuilder). New Source options and a Job board filter on Requirements. Requirements saved before keep "Pasted" and their text.
  • Ignore on one job is kept: in a job-board alert, Add and Ignore are stored per job (team inbox and My book), so an ignored job stays ignored after a reload and on your teammates' screens. Ignored jobs fold under "Show N ignored jobs" with Move back. Each alert shows "N added, M ignored, K left". Two teammates can no longer add the same job twice. My book stores only the job's number and status; the email stays encrypted.
  • Morning email: "M added as requirements" now counts every requirement made from the inbox (an alert with 5 jobs counts 5), not the emails.

Admin: team scorecard and remote config (backlog S6, S7)

  • Admin → Teams (scorecard): one row per team with plan and pilot state, days left, members, members active in the last 7 days (signed in or did something in the team), requirements and submissions this week, guard warnings (the duplicate-submission guard showed a match) and overrides, team inbox use, and the last morning report sent. Sortable by any column. Counts and dates only, never anything from a team's book. The guard did not record its warnings before; it now adds one to a per-team daily counter (no consultant, client or user stored).

Team web app: desks / offices for Agency (backlog W10)

  • Desks (Team → Desks, Agency and the pilot; Starter and Team see an upgrade note): owners and managers add desks with an optional office or location, seat each recruiter on one desk, and can put a consultant on a desk of their own (otherwise a consultant counts on their recruiter's desk). At most 50 per team.
  • Filter by desk on Bench, Requirements, Submissions, Matches and the activity log, plus "No desk". Bench shows each consultant's desk.
  • Morning report per desk: once a team has desks, the "By desk" lines (yesterday and the weekly summary) are one per desk, "Desk name (Office)", plus "No desk"; without desks they stay one per recruiter.

Vendor book: job changes in the drawer and a timeline per vendor (backlog E5, Vendor Book slice 4)

  • Job-change banner in the drawer: when a recruiter on a drawer card (or the LinkedIn profile you opened) has a pending job-change suggestion, the card shows it with Update contact / Merge, keep the new email / Not the same person and Undo. Same words and same rules as the dashboard's Vendor book card; Update and Merge are Solo (the worker refuses them on Free), "Not the same person" is free. Opening a saved recruiter's profile that names a new company shows the banner at once.
  • Timeline per vendor (Vendors → open a vendor): posts from the post log, recruiters added, updated (from a post, by you), moved here or moved away, submissions and replies, newest first, with All / Posts / Contacts / Submissions filters. Computed, nothing stored.
  • One merge path for job changes: the dashboard and the drawer both merge through the new MERGE_MOVE message, which takes the pair from the stored suggestion (not from the message).

Inboxes: job-board alerts split into their jobs (backlog E16)

  • "N jobs from Dice": a job alert forwarded to the team inbox or to My book's personal inbox from Dice, Indeed, LinkedIn Job Alerts, ZipRecruiter, Monster or CareerBuilder now lists its jobs (title, company, location, rate, posted day, the job's link) instead of being read as one requirement. Each job has Add, Ignore (hides it on the screen) and Open the job; Add all takes up to 100 jobs. Recognised by the sender, a hand-forwarded "From:" line, the subject or the board's job links; works on both the text and the HTML form of the email.
  • Team inbox: each job becomes its own requirement with the job's link and the board named in its text, through the same claim as "Add to requirements" (a teammate who added the email first stops the add before anything is saved). A job already in Requirements (same link) is skipped. The email is marked added once at least one job went in.
  • My book (Solo): a job that names a recruiter's email goes in as that recruiter, with the board and the job link; a job with no recruiter email says so (the book keeps recruiters, so it cannot hold a job without one). Still read in your browser only: the personal inbox stays end-to-end encrypted.
  • No-reply senders are never a contact: the boards' alert and no-reply mailboxes (jobalerts-noreply@…, alert@indeed.com, any address on a board's domain) are no longer taken as the vendor contact, on the generic path too.

Overnight follow-ups (14 Nov): résumé files of a deleted consultant, interview hold in the morning email, location read from a post

  • Fix (team server): résumé files stayed stored after their consultant was deleted. Every removed résumé version (a deleted consultant, a deleted version, the last-5 prune, the workspace purge) now queues its file, and the report function's 15-minute tick deletes it through the Storage API, retrying until it goes.
  • Fix (morning email): "No submission this week" still listed consultants In interview, while the web app's Today screen holds them out. The email and the per-desk rows now leave them out the same way and add one line: "In interview (held out of this list): N".

"Bring BenchPilot to your team" from the popup and the dashboard (backlog E14, entry part)

  • Popup: a small "Bring BenchPilot to your team" line under More. It opens the new Settings card in the dashboard. The × hides it for 30 days, and so does copying the message or the link. It shows only when you are signed in and not in a team, and never while the open tab is LinkedIn.
  • Dashboard → Settings → Bring your team: the same card as on the plans page (Get my team link, Copy message, Copy link, Make a new link). Only for signed-in users who are not in a team. Deep link: #settings?section=team.
  • One flow: the plans page and the dashboard both run upgrade/bring-team.js. BenchPilot still never sends the note: you copy it and send it yourself. The reward rules and the server are unchanged.
  • The "hidden for 30 days" time is a local flag (bp_bring_team_hidden_at). It is not in backups and not synced.

Encrypted sync phase 2: resume files, a sync chip in the popup, a sync slide in the tour (backlog E2, E3)

  • Resume files sync, encrypted (with sync on): the resumes attached to consultants and your own resume are encrypted on your computer, each with its own random key, and uploaded to a private storage bucket. The server holds the locked file, an id and its size; the file name, the consultant and the key travel only inside your encrypted data. Another computer brings missing files down a few at a time in the background; deletions and renames follow. Limits: 5 MB a file, 200 MB and 1,000 files an account (separate from the 50 MB for the rest of your data); over them a file stays on its computer and Settings says so.
  • "Replace my keys" re-wraps the file keys with the new key and does not re-upload files, unless you tick "Also re-encrypt resume files" (you see the file count and size first): then every file gets a new key and is uploaded again, and the old copies are deleted. File keys are stored on your computer only encrypted with your sync key.
  • Turning sync off (typed DELETE) also deletes every synced file from the server; the files stay on your computer. Files of accounts removed after 60 days without a plan, or deleted, are removed by the daily server tick.
  • Sync chip in the popup: Synced / Syncing… / Sync locked / Sync paused / Sync problem; click to open Settings, Sync. Hidden while sync is off.
  • First-run tour: a fifth slide, "Yours, on every computer. Only you can read it.", shown only when sync is switched on in this build and the plan includes it.
  • Backups are unchanged (the files were already in them; the new sync bookkeeping is not).

Drawer polish, and the "LinkedIn may have changed" warning works again (backlog E4, E6)

  • One meaning for "Matches": it is the tab's name only. The header number is now Good fits and the Requirements chip Good fit (14 days).
  • Late follow-ups are red (dot and the words "N days late"); due-today ones keep the quiet dot.
  • One Clear: with a header number acting as a filter, the Matches tab showed both "Clear" and "Show everything" for the same thing. Only the Showing bar's Clear is left.
  • Contrast: the small note under the duplicate-submission check is drawn at full strength (it was 4.1:1, under the 4.5:1 minimum).
  • Calmer motion: the green "live" dot pulses three times and stops (it pulsed forever); the drawer width, tab underline, sheets and toast ease out instead of overshooting. Reduce motion (system or Settings) still turns all of it off.
  • Fix: the capture warning could never fire. The "BenchPilot can see requirement posts here but could not read the recruiter emails" warning counted only posts the parser had already accepted, so "seen but nothing read" was impossible. It now counts visible emails in requirement-like posts before the parser's own checks. Found by the new tests below.
  • Tests on saved feed pages: the real content script now runs in the tests on five sanitized LinkedIn feed pages (fictional people, example.com emails): normal feed with a comment email, a re-share, mailto and "[at] [dot]" addresses, a redesigned layout, and a page whose selectors broke (the warning must fire). A small test-only DOM (tests/helpers/mini-dom.js) means no npm install is needed in CI. Nothing new is packaged.

Team web app: email templates with the company signature, and "Draft email" (backlog W7)

  • Email templates (Team → Email templates, #templates): pitch, follow-up, hotlist intro and check-in templates for the whole team. Owners and managers add, edit and delete them; everyone uses them. A team starts with the extension's own pitch, submit and hotlist templates plus a follow-up and a check-in, saved for the team the first time an owner or manager opens the screen. At most 40 per team.
  • Same placeholders and the same filling as the extension ({firstName}, {requirement}, {consultantName} ...): the web app runs the extension's fillTemplate / fillSubmitEmail and buildComposeUrl, not a copy.
  • Company signature: company name and website (owners and managers), plus each member's own name, job title and phone (only that member sees them). Plain text under every draft, no images.
  • Draft email on Requirements, Matches, Submissions ("Draft follow-up") and Today's follow-ups: pick a template and a consultant, check the text, then Open in Gmail or Open in Outlook. The draft opens in your own account; nothing is sent from BenchPilot. A vendor contact or company marked Do not contact in the team book blocks the draft with a message.

Team vendor book: smart lists and the email check (backlog W5, W6)

  • Smart lists in the team vendor book (web app, Team, Agency and the pilot; Starter sees an upgrade note): the extension's four built-in lists (Hot now, Cold 60+ days, Replied in 30 days, Missing phone) as buttons with counts above the table, plus lists the team saves ("+ Save a list": heat, role hired, replied in 30 / 90 days, no requirement for 30 / 60 / 90+ days, phone). A list is a rule, not a set of names, so it stays current. Counted and filtered by the extension's own BP.VendorBook.evaluateList over the team book. Saved lists belong to the team: everyone sees them, owners and managers save and delete them, up to 25 per team.

Team web app: same role from several vendors, full requirement tags, interview hold (backlog W2, W3, W4)

  • Same role from N vendors: the same requirement posted by several vendors (same job ID, or the same title and end client within 14 days, the extension's own v1.18 rule) is one row in Requirements, one card in Matches and one follow-up on Today, marked "Same role from N vendors" with the other vendors listed. "Show the same role once" can be turned off. Worked out in the browser
  • Full requirement tags: visas the post takes and rules out, tax terms (C2C, W2, 1099), work mode, rate from-to per hour/day/week/month/year and duration in months, set in the paste form (read with the extension's parser), a new "Add a requirement" form and a new "Edit". New filters: visa it takes, USC / GC only, tax terms, work mode, pays at least per hour, at least N months
  • Interview hold: a consultant "In interview" is held out of Matches and of Today's "no submission this week" lists; "Show held" brings them back, marked

Team web app and server: activity log for owners and managers, and the automatic purge of closed workspaces (backlog W8, S3)

  • Activity log (Team settings → Open the activity log, #audit): who added, changed or deleted what, as plain lines ("Asha changed submission Ravi Kumar at Cobalt Energy (stage: submitted to interview)"). Filter by person, type and date range; 50 per page with Older / Newer; Export this list as CSV when the workspace's export setting allows the role. Owners and managers only. The log keeps ids only; names come from the team's own book, and no email or phone is ever shown or exported.
  • Closed workspaces are deleted for good 30 days after they close. 23 days after a workspace closes (by its owner, or after 30 days read-only unpaid) the owner gets one warning email with the date; at least 7 days later every team record (bench and résumés, vendor book, contacts, requirements, submissions, activity log, team inbox, members, invites) and its stored files are deleted. Workspaces with paid time left, an extended pilot or one re-opened by support are never deleted. A tombstone keeps only the team id, dates and row counts; payments stay for the accounts.

Paste a requirement, and "Draft email" opens the email (backlog E1, E8 / K4)

  • Paste a requirement (every plan): on the dashboard's Requirements page (and from Today), paste a requirement from an email, WhatsApp or a job board, press *Read the fields*, check and edit them (role, end client, job ID, rate, tax terms, location, work mode, visa, duration, skills, recruiter email, name, phone, vendor), and save. It is saved with its recruiter through the same save path as a LinkedIn save (marked "Pasted requirement"), then matched to the bench like any other requirement. An email on the Don't email list can be saved, but no draft opens to it. Nothing leaves the computer.
  • "Draft email for <consultant>" in the Requirements table opens the email draft (through the single draft gate, so the Don't email list applies). It used to open the requirement's panel and only highlight the consultant (K4).

Team web app and server: resume upload for team consultants (backlog W1)

  • Resumes on the Consultant page. Anyone in the team can upload a PDF or Word (.docx) resume, up to 5 MB, checked in the browser with the extension's own file check before anything is sent. The last 5 versions are kept (newest = current); Open (PDF) and Download (.docx) use links that work for one minute. Owners and managers can delete a version. Read-only workspaces can still open files but not add or delete them.
  • Private storage per team: one private bucket, a folder per team and consultant; only active members of that team can read or upload (a removed member loses access at once), no file is ever overwritten. The activity log records ids only. The demo workspace keeps file names only, never files.

Team web app and server: vendor heat, whole-bench matches, follow-ups, weekly and per-desk reports (spec docs/specs/TEAM_P2_SPEC.md)

  • Vendor book heat and response stats (Team, Agency, pilot): each vendor company is Hot, Active or Cold by the same rules as the extension's Vendor Book, from the team's requirements and submissions, with submissions sent and reply, interview and placement rates over 30 and 90 days. Filter by heat or sort hottest first. Starter sees an upgrade note.
  • Matches (every plan): every open requirement against the whole bench, and every consultant against the open requirements, with the extension's match score (60 % and up). A pair someone on the team already submitted in the last 90 days is marked "Already submitted by <name>" and listed last; "New submission" opens the form filled in, and the guard still runs.
  • Follow-ups on Today (every plan): submissions with no update after 24 hours (vendor) or 48 hours (client), and requirements with no submission after 24 hours. Recruiters see their own; owners and managers see everyone's. Nothing is emailed.
  • Weekly summary in the morning report (Team, Agency, pilot) on the day the owner picks in Team settings (default Monday): the last 7 days' submissions (and the week before), stage moves, new requirements and vendors, guard overrides. Per-desk lines (Agency, pilot): each recruiter's submissions, interviews and bench, daily and for the week. Counts and the firm's own recruiter names only; no vendor names, emails or phones.

Today's homework: your daily plan (spec docs/specs/TODAY_HOMEWORK_SPEC.md)

  • A to-do list for the day, written from what BenchPilot already knows. New strong matches saved this shift, follow-ups due (and drafts not yet marked as sent), consultants on the bench 30+ days with no submission this week, things to check in the Vendor Book, and a backup once 50+ recruiters are saved. At most 12 open items, money first.
  • Where: a Today card at the top of the drawer's Matches tab ("6 things for today · 2 done", with a progress bar) that opens the list in a sheet, and the first block of the dashboard's Today page.
  • One click each: a row opens the match card, the follow-up, the consultant's best match (or Find recruiters), the Vendor Book or Backup. Opening a match ticks it; the rest tick themselves when the thing happens and stay on the list, ticked, until the next day. Tick by hand, or Tomorrow to snooze.
  • The day starts at 6:00 pm IST (dashboard Today → "My day starts at"), so a shift past midnight is one day. "Nothing left for today" names the next start; a quiet "N days in a row" counts emptied lists. No desktop notifications; the toolbar badge is unchanged.
  • Solo: check-in drafts for *Trusted* vendors that have not answered a submission for 14+ days (opens in your mail app, never sent by BenchPilot; "Skip this week"), and yesterday's numbers at the top (requirements saved, submissions sent, vendor replies, interviews, homework done), computed on your computer. Free sees how many quiet vendors there are.

Vendor Book, part 2: job changes, saved smart lists, "Merge safe ones" (spec docs/specs/VENDOR_BOOK_SPEC.md, slices 2 and 3)

  • Job changes. When a saved recruiter posts from a new company's email with the same LinkedIn profile or phone and the same name, or you open their LinkedIn profile and it names a new company, the Vendor book card shows a suggestion with both emails and the evidence. Update contact moves the email, company and title (notes, status, follow-up date and activity stay; the old email is kept as an earlier email; a title or phone you typed stays yours) with Undo; Merge when both emails are saved; Not the same person hides it for good. Nothing changes by itself, a name alone or a Gmail / Yahoo address never counts, and nothing is clicked or opened on LinkedIn. Update and Merge are Solo; seeing and dismissing are free. No reveal, no new contact.
  • Saved smart lists (Solo). "+ Save this view" on Vendors and Recruiters keeps the filters as a list (up to 25), with a live count. Rules only, never names; a list that refers to a removed role group shows 0 and a note and is never deleted. New "Hires" filter on Vendors. Free keeps the four built-in lists, and lists saved on Solo keep working after a plan ends. In backups and encrypted sync.
  • Export this list: the list's recruiters as a CSV (Solo, like every export); people on your Don't email list are left out.
  • Merge safe ones: duplicates with the same LinkedIn profile or the same name at the same company (never a phone alone) merge in one go, up to 25 groups, after a preview, with one Undo for the whole batch (until the next batch or browser restart). Solo.
  • Popup: "Vendor book: N to check" when something needs a decision.

Vendor Book: your vendor book keeps itself up to date (spec docs/specs/VENDOR_BOOK_SPEC.md, slice 1 plus the built-in lists)

  • Saved recruiters update themselves from the posts you scroll past. "Last seen in a post", a missing title, phone or LinkedIn profile fills in at once, and a *different* title or phone is changed only after two different posts show it (a fallback like "Recruiter" never replaces a real title; a switchboard number shared by 40+ recruiters is ignored). No reveal, no new contact, nothing clicked or opened on LinkedIn.
  • Every change can be undone. The recruiter's panel has a Vendor book section: when they were last seen, the roles they hire for, and each change BenchPilot made with a Restore button. A title, phone or profile you type by hand is yours: BenchPilot never changes it (with a "Let BenchPilot update it" link).
  • Heat per vendor on Vendors and in the drawer: Hot (3+ posts in 30 days, or 2 in 14, or a reply / interview in 30 days with a post), Active (a post in 60 days), Cold (quiet 60+ days). Filter and sort by Heat. "Hires: Java / J2EE (7), Data engineer (3)" under each vendor (last 90 days). Your Trusted / Avoid labels are never changed.
  • Vendor book health card at the top of Vendors: possible duplicates, gone cold, no phone, no vendor, looks like a bench seller, name doesn't match email, marked bounced, and "N contacts updated from posts this week" with Restore. Counts are free; the fixes are the existing Fix my data actions (Solo). The drawer's Vendors tab shows "N things to check in your vendor book".
  • Built-in lists on Vendors: Hot now, Cold 60+ days, Replied in 30 days, Missing phone. Always current; nothing stored.

Hotlist builder (spec docs/specs/HOTLIST_BUILDER_SPEC.md)

  • Hotlist on the Bench page replaces the old "Copy hotlist" menu. Tick the consultants (the active ones are ticked), choose the columns and their order (role, experience, top skills, visa, location, terms, rate, availability) and how names show (first name + last initial by default, initials or full name). BenchPilot remembers your choice.
  • Outputs: Copy text (an email with a subject line), Copy table (a table you paste into Gmail or Outlook; plain text where the browser cannot copy a table), Excel, CSV, and Open draft (subject and text, no recipients: you pick them in your mail app; the Don't email list applies). A consultant's phone, email, notes and resume never go in. BenchPilot never sends email.
  • Part of Solo. Free shows a preview of 3 consultants with "Upgrade to Solo"; the per-consultant hotlist line in Copy pitch stays free.
  • Team web app: a Hotlist button on Bench builds the same text, table and CSV from the firm's bench (Marketing consultants ticked; the CSV follows the workspace export setting).

Find recruiters for a consultant, mail-merge export, do-not-email list (spec docs/specs/RECRUITERS_FOR_CONSULTANT_SPEC.md)

  • Find recruiters on each consultant (Bench page, Match workspace, and the consultant's card in the LinkedIn drawer). It opens Export by role prefilled from the profile: role family from the title (or skills), their top 3 skills, the last 90 days, one row per recruiter. The preview says "12 recruiters at 7 vendors posted roles like Ravi's in the last 90 days". Opening it and the preview are free; downloads need Solo, like every export.
  • Export for mail merge: a CSV for Gmail mail-merge tools (Email, First name, Full name, Company, Contact type, Role group, Last role they posted, Last seen, Phone), one row per address, newest first. A note above the button: send from your own account, add an opt-out line, stop when asked. BenchPilot never sends email.
  • Don't email list (free): on Vendors → Recruiters (and the lead panel's More menu), mark a person "Don't email" with a reason (asked to stop, bounced, not relevant), with Undo. BenchPilot then opens no draft to them anywhere (Submit sheet, Draft email, follow-ups, plain Email, the Match workspace), leaves them out of mail-merge files and "Copy emails", and adds a "Do not email" column to the Recruiters exports. A chip shows on the recruiter row and in the drawer's contact line.
  • Contact types (Tech recruiter / Company HR / Bench sales) are the ones from v1.12, so the finder's type ticks and the "Contact type" column use the same rules and your own changes.

BenchPilot Solo: one paid plan, and Free saves unlimited contacts (decision F6; spec docs/specs/SOLO_PLAN_SPEC.md)

  • Free saves unlimited recruiter contacts (before: 25 a month) and keeps up to 3 consultants (before: 2). The monthly contact meter, its "contacts left" lines and the autosave pause no longer appear, because no plan has a monthly limit.
  • Solo replaces Basic and Pro: ₹499 a month or ₹3,999 a year ($12 / $99 shown outside India; checkout in rupees). Founding price ₹399 a month for the first 100 buyers, for 12 months. Solo has everything Pro had plus encrypted sync across computers.
  • Basic and Pro holders keep their plan until it ends, and renew as Solo ("Renew as Solo"); leftover days convert by price.
  • The upgrade page shows Free and Solo, the compare table has two columns, and every "Upgrade" button says "Upgrade to Solo".

Web app: My book for Solo (spec docs/specs/SOLO_WEB_WORKSPACE_SPEC.md)

  • Open your own book in the web app. Sign in with the same account as in the extension, enter your sync passphrase (or recovery code), and see your recruiters, vendors, consultants, submissions, notes and jobs, with search and filters. It is decrypted in your browser tab only; the server still only holds encrypted data.
  • Small changes from any computer: a recruiter's status, notes and follow-up date; a consultant's title, skills, visa, rate, location, availability, notes and active switch. They are encrypted in the tab and reach the extension on its next sync; changes made in the extension at the same time are kept.
  • The book locks itself on sign-out, when the tab closes and after 30 minutes without activity. Without Solo the page shows "Upgrade to Solo" (buying stays in the extension).

Solo: your own inbox address, encrypted on arrival (spec docs/specs/SOLO_INBOX_SPEC.md)

  • Forward requirement emails to your own BenchPilot address (p-…@<our mail domain>), made in the web app under My book > Inbox; turn it off or replace it there. The extension shows it in Settings > Sync with a Copy button.
  • Only you can read them: each email is encrypted the moment it arrives, with a key only your browser can open (your sync passphrase). The server keeps only the encrypted email, when it arrived, its size and whether you added or ignored it.
  • Add to my book turns an email into a recruiter in your encrypted book (read with the same requirement reader as "Paste a requirement"); Ignore and Open the email as in the team inbox; the Gmail forwarding code is shown at the top.
  • Limits: 500 emails a day, 50 MB; emails are deleted after 90 days (30 days after Ignore). Turning sync off deletes the inbox.
  • "Replace my keys" moves the inbox key to the new keys in the same step.

Version 1.19.0 12 November 2026

Vendor memory and follow-through (v1.19)

  • Every post a saved recruiter makes is kept. Before, a second requirement from a recruiter you had already saved was dropped. Now BenchPilot keeps up to 50 later posts per recruiter (role, posted date, location, skills, rate, link to the post), on your computer only. The lead panel on the dashboard shows them under Posts from this recruiter ("12 posts saved, 4 in the last 30 days"). No contact is used up for this, and with autosave off it still learns about recruiters you already saved.
  • Later posts are matched too. Each one is a requirement of its own on Matches, Today and the Match workspace, with the same rules as before: last 14 days, closed or stale posts out, already submitted or dismissed for a consultant out.
  • One question on first use: how should recruiters be saved? New users are asked once in the LinkedIn drawer: "I'll pick each one" or "Save every recruiter I see". The Autosave switch in the toolbar button changes it later.
  • The drawer and Matches agree. When matching posts on the page are not saved yet, Matches says how many and offers to save them, instead of looking empty. The Requirements "Matches" chip now says 14 days, the same window Matches uses.
  • Draft email, then Mark as sent. BenchPilot opens an email draft and cannot know whether you sent it. The submission now waits as not marked as sent (the Already submitted? check still counts it) until you tap Mark as sent (drawer, or Follow-ups due on Today). The follow-up date counts from that day. Not sent closes it. Older submissions count as sent.
  • Merging duplicate contacts moves their posts to the kept contact (Undo puts them back); editing a contact's email keeps its posts.

Matches you can trust (v1.18)

  • Honest match scores. Must-have skills (the ones in the post's title and skills line, or under "must have / required") count double, so a missing one costs points. Visa (the post's allowed and not-allowed lists), C2C / W2 terms, rate (when both the post and the consultant have one) and how new the post is are now scored. A part that is not known earns only a few points, never full marks. Expect a real spread (for example 92, 81, 67) instead of a wall of 95 to 98 %. The 60 % line is unchanged.
  • Why this score. The drawer's "Why N%" panel lists the points per part (skills, title, location, experience, visa, terms, rate, posted) and says which parts were not known. The dashboard's match evidence says the same.
  • Same role from many vendors, one card in the drawer. Posts with the same job ID, or the same title and end client within 14 days, show as one card: the best vendor first (Trusted, then Prime / Tier 1, then the best match), "Same role from N vendors" and a "Show all" link. Same rule as the Match workspace.
  • "Needs a look". Posts BenchPilot could not read clearly (unclear post type, maybe a job seeker, or no skills readable) carry a "Needs a look" label, are never a strong match (75 %+), stay out of the drawer's Matches list and have their own "Needs a look" list behind More.
  • Recruiter type filter on the dashboard, and one shared filter state: Terms and recruiter Type chosen in the drawer, on Requirements or in the Match workspace carry over to the others.
  • New Requirements filters: a visa the post takes, rate (stated, not stated, up to $50/h, $50 to $70/h, $70/h and up), end client (named, confidential, not stated), contacted or not, company email or free mail (Gmail, Yahoo and others), and closes in 3, 7 or 14 days. Saved views keep them.

Team web app: import, export, settings, delete (pilot)

  • Import from Excel or CSV. Owners and managers drop an .xlsx or .csv file; columns are matched with the extension's own import rules, the first 20 rows of each sheet are shown, then "Import N vendors, M consultants" and a summary. Vendor contacts merge by email (companies by email domain), consultants by name; existing records only get empty fields filled.
  • Export everything. The bench, vendor companies, contacts, requirements and submissions as CSV files in one .zip. The owner can always export; managers and recruiters only when the export policy allows, checked on the server.
  • Workspace settings save in your own workspace: name, morning report time and time zone (your browser's zone by default), and who can export. Owner only.
  • Delete workspace with the typed workspace name (owner only). Everyone loses access at once; the data is kept so support can undo it.
  • Requirements: skill, work mode and tax-term tags in the list, a Source filter (extension, pasted, import), and the job reference from a pasted requirement is now kept in your own workspace.

Team billing and the 14-day pilot

  • Plan and billing in Team settings. The owner sees the current plan, the days left and a Pay button for Starter, Team and Agency (prices come from the server). Paying adds one month from the day the current plan or pilot ends. US teams see "Pay by invoice" until US dollar payments are switched on.
  • Pilot reminder. From day 12 of the 14-day pilot (and 2 days before a paid month ends) the owner gets an email and everyone sees a banner with a link to pay.
  • Read-only after the plan ends. If the plan is not paid, the workspace becomes read-only for 30 days: everyone can still see and export everything, but nothing can be added or changed. After that it is closed and marked for deletion, with an email to the owner.
  • One more pilot fortnight on request. The owner can ask for 14 more days once; Nick grants it.
  • The demo workspace shows a sample pilot on day 12.

Team morning report (pilot)

  • Morning report email to the workspace owner at the report time (default 08:00, India time): yesterday's submissions by recruiter, interviews, consultants with no submission this week, bench over 30 days, new vendors and guard warnings people went past. Only your own consultants and recruiters are named; no vendor emails or phones. One "Open BenchPilot" button. Sent at most once a day; a failed send is retried (up to 3 tries) and never sent more than 6 hours late.
  • "Also send the morning report to managers" in Team settings (off by default).
  • Today shows "Last morning report: <date>, sent/failed".

Clean data (v1.17)

  • The whole post is read. A long post cut at "…see more" is now read in full (what LinkedIn already has on the page; BenchPilot still clicks nothing), so the role, rate, client and visa further down are picked up.
  • Job seekers are kept apart. People looking for a job who post their own email (#OpenToWork, "I am looking for a new role", "my resume") are not treated as recruiters: they are left out of matches, Radar and Today, and listed under Candidates in Requirements (Post type filter). When BenchPilot is not sure, the contact shows a "Check: recruiter or job seeker?" label.
  • Settings → Fix my data → Possible job seekers finds them among what you already saved. Move them to Candidates or keep them as recruiters, one at a time or all clear cases at once, with Undo.
  • Job seekers and team mailboxes don't use up your monthly contacts.
  • Team mailboxes (hr@, jobs@, info@) get a "Team mailbox" label and are never given a made-up person name such as "Hr".
  • Unknown stays unknown. Vendor tier and client type are left blank when the post does not say, instead of a made-up "Tier 1" and "Direct Client". Saved records are cleaned the same way. Settings → Defaults has a "Leave blank" choice; a default you pick is still used.
  • Closed and old requirements drop out of matches. A post that says the position is filled or closed, a passed deadline, or a post older than 30 days is no longer matched, and shows a "Closed", "Deadline passed" or "Old" label.
  • One set of matches everywhere. The drawer, Radar, Today, the Bench and the Match workspace all use the same requirements: the last 14 days, not closed, and not already submitted or skipped for that consultant. The Match workspace opens on 14 days (7 and 30 days are one click away).
  • Fixed: wrong "posted" dates. A job tenure such as "1 yr" or "11 mos" near the post, or the time on a comment or a re-shared post, was read as the post's age, so some requirements showed a 2025 date. Those dates are now ignored, and saved records with such a date fall back to the day you saved them.

Added

  • A Match workspace for each consultant. On the Bench, "482 matching requirements" now opens a full-width page instead of a narrow list inside the card. Your consultants are on the left with how many new matches each has. The matches are in the middle, as short rows with the title, the company and recruiter, the score, how long ago it was posted and where you are with it. The requirement you pick opens on the right in full: title, company, end client, location, rate and terms, why it matches (what the consultant has, what is missing, what blocks it), the recruiter with their contact buttons, and the whole post to read and scroll. You never leave the page to read a post. It has its own address, #matches-<consultant>, and Today's match links open it too. On a smaller window the requirement slides in over the list; on a phone it fills the screen with a Back button.
  • Remember what you did with each match. Every match is New, Pitched, Submitted, Skipped or Not relevant, for that consultant. Draft email opens the draft in your mail app and marks it Pitched (you still press Send; BenchPilot sends nothing, and it is not counted as a submission). Mark submitted records the submission with the "Already submitted?" check, and asks for a reason if you are about to submit the same role twice. Skip and Not relevant clear it from your list. Every action has an Undo in the message that appears. To do, Pitched, Submitted and Skipped are tabs; only To do is open by default, so you see what is left.
  • It opens on what matters. To do, posted in the last 7 days, with what BenchPilot saved since your last visit on top and a line saying "9 new since your last visit". Chips for Posted (today, 3 days, 7 days, 30 days, any age), Remote or Local, Terms (C2C, W2, Full-time), Type (bench sales are left out unless you ask) and "Not yet submitted". BenchPilot remembers your choices.
  • Better order than every card saying 95%. Matches are ordered by score, then by the day they were posted (newest first), then by vendor: Prime vendors, Tier 1, Tier 2, others, and vendors you labelled Avoid last. Each row has a short line saying why ("Java, Spring Boot · same role · Remote").
  • The same role from several vendors is one row. "Same role from 3 vendors" opens to show each vendor with their tier, recruiter, age and rate, so you pick whose post to answer. Same title and same end client, or the same job ID, posted within 14 days of each other. If you already submitted that role through one vendor, the others say so.
  • Keyboard: J and K move, Enter opens, E drafts the email, S marks it submitted, X skips, U undoes, / searches. The shortcuts are listed at the bottom of the page.

Version 1.16.0 10 November 2026

Added

  • Who posted it: Tech recruiter, Bench sales or Company HR. BenchPilot reads the post, the poster's headline and the company label, and puts a small chip on each recruiter in the LinkedIn drawer and in the dashboard Recruiters list. A headline such as "US IT Bench Sales" or "Bench Marketing" marks a bench sales contact, even when the post is a requirement. A company called "Bench Sales Inc" does not make its recruiters bench sales.
  • Change the type in one click. Click the chip and pick Tech recruiter, Bench sales or Company HR. Your choice always wins. When you pick Bench sales, BenchPilot asks whether to mark the other contacts at that company the same way.
  • A Type filter: All, Technical recruiters, Bench sales, Company HR, in the drawer's Requirements tab and the dashboard Recruiters list. BenchPilot remembers your choice. Bench sales contacts stay in their own list: they never show in your pitch list or in matches. Contacts BenchPilot could not tell count as technical recruiters.
  • A Type filter in exports. Export by role and the Recruiters export have the same three boxes. Technical recruiters and Company HR are ticked, Bench sales is not, and every file has a Contact type column.
  • "A LinkedIn group" as an answer to "How did you hear about BenchPilot?", on the welcome page and on the page you see after removing BenchPilot.
  • Two optional follow-up boxes on the page after you remove BenchPilot. Pick "I use something else" and it asks "What do you use instead?". Pick "Other" and it asks "What was the reason?". Both are up to 300 characters, optional and sent without your name or email.

Changed

  • The Bench sellers chip hidden under More in the drawer is replaced by the Type filter's Bench sales button, so it is easy to find.
  • "Mark as bench seller" on a card and in the recruiter panel is now the Type chip and the Type buttons.
  • The old "Include bench sellers" box in Export by role is now the Bench sales box in the Type filter.

Version 1.15.0 9 November 2026

Added

  • Tax terms on every consultant: C2C, W2, 1099 or Any. Pick it where you add or edit a consultant (the welcome page and the Bench). The consultant card shows it.
  • W2 matches. A W2 consultant is matched to W2 posts and to posts that don't state any terms. Posts that say C2C or 1099 only are left out, and so are full-time posts (unless the post also says W2 contract). "Any" matches C2C, W2 and 1099 posts. The reason line says "W2 ok" next to the other reasons.

  • "I mostly work on" (C2C, W2 or Both) in Settings, and as a question in the welcome page ("Do you work on C2C, W2 or both?"). It sets the tax terms a new consultant starts with and the Terms filter you start on. It stays on your computer.

Changed

  • Everyone you already have stays on C2C, so nothing changes for existing consultants until you change their tax terms.

Version 1.14.0 6 November 2026

Added

  • Email verification by 6-digit code (AUTH_VERIFY_CODE). The link in the email still works.
  • Prices in US dollars on the plans page for visitors outside India ($4.99 Basic, $9.99 Pro), with a ₹ / $ switch. Checkout is still in rupees through Razorpay.

Changed

  • A free account is now part of setup for new installs, with Google or with email and a code.

Version 1.13.0 28 October 2026

Added

The page asks three optional questions: why they removed it (6 reasons), what would have made them keep it, and how they heard about BenchPilot. Answers arrive as an anonymous Idea in admin → Feedback, with only the version number attached.

Headers, top bars, dialogs and the dashboard sidebar are now white with a thin divider instead of purple bands. The header numbers are plain instead of yellow on dark plates. Cards are outlined instead of shadowed, and chips are quiet outlines. The Trusted / Avoid switch uses soft tints. The upgrade page's main button is purple. Nothing moved and no feature changed.

It leads with recruiter contacts by role (growth plan Step 2, approved by Nick on 26 Oct). The full store text is in store-assets/STORE_LISTING_v1.13.0.md.

Version 1.12.0 22 October 2026

Added

  • Choose autosave on the welcome page: "Save every recruiter automatically (uses your monthly contacts)" or "I'll pick each one". Skipping keeps it off, and the welcome text now says so.
  • First-5-minutes checklist on the welcome page and dashboard Today. It ticks itself: add a consultant, choose autosave, open LinkedIn, see a match, draft an email. Existing users never see it after updating.
  • Help guide (help/help.html): how BenchPilot works, where things live, a glossary and an FAQ. Open it from popup → More → Help, the "?" in the drawer, or Settings → Help.
  • Due follow-ups on the toolbar icon (Basic and Pro): the badge shows how many follow-ups are due today or overdue.
  • "Back up now" in the popup once you have 50+ recruiters and no backup this week. The backup reminder can't be snoozed for longer than 3 days at that size.

Changed

"Submit <name>" is Draft email for <name>, and the done screen says the submission was logged when the draft opened. The duplicate guard is the "Already submitted?" check. Cleanup is Fix my data. "Vendor type" is Vendor tier (or Client type for the end-client field). Recruiter means the person and requirement means the post, everywhere. Exports use the new column names.
  • Popup is a doorway: your numbers, the scanner and autosave switches, "Open LinkedIn" and "Open dashboard". Everything else is under More, and nothing was removed.
  • Matches agrees with Requirements: when posts are on the page but none are saved, the Matches tab says "3 requirements on this page, none saved yet" and offers "Save these 3".
  • JSON export is included from Basic in the popup too, as decided on 16 Oct.
  • Clearer messages for failed loads, saves, restores and licence keys. Empty Submissions and Vendors screens now say what to do next. Posts without a name or company show "Name not shown" / "Company not shown".
  • Store summary no longer says "never double-submit".
  • Fonts on LinkedIn load through a per-session address, so pages cannot detect BenchPilot by probing a fixed font URL.
  • Drawer header is lighter: pause, settings and report a bug are now under one More (⋯) button, and the header has four icons instead of seven. A yellow dot on More shows when the scanner is paused. The keyboard-shortcuts button at the bottom is now a keyboard icon, so the drawer has only one "?" (Help).
  • Matches opens on the matches: "Already submitted?" warnings are compact rows under the matches instead of big red boxes above them. A card with a red or yellow button says why on the card itself ("Already submitted to Halcyon Motors via Brightpath Staffing on 18 Oct").
  • Two consultants with the same first name are told apart everywhere in the drawer: "Draft email for Ravi K." and "Ravi T." instead of two "Ravi"s.

Fixed

  • Posts shown because a connection commented were missed: when LinkedIn shows a post with a line like "Riya V commented" (no "on this"), BenchPilot took the commenter for the author, and the real recruiter's requirement could be dropped. Now the commenter is skipped and the post is captured under the recruiter who wrote it. The same goes for "reposted", "replied" and "reacted". Posts that say "Job Role" or "required skillset" also count as requirements now. (Found from Nick's 22 Oct screenshot.)
  • Search finds a company typed as one word: "softsnippets" now finds "Soft Snippets INC", also when the recruiter's email is hidden because the month's contacts are used up.
  • Matches is never an empty list under a count: when the only matches are from vendors you marked Avoid, the tab says so and points to Show all.

Excel puts each dataset on its own sheet, and several CSVs come as one ZIP. Consultant files never include résumé files. The free Backup & restore is unchanged and is still the way to move your data between computers.

  • Plans now say "CSV, Excel and JSON export" for Basic and Pro (#158). JSON export is no longer listed as Pro-only, here or in the Terms.
  • Exported cells that start with =, +, - or @ can't run as spreadsheet formulas (#158).

Version 1.7.0 8 October 2026

Version 1.6.1 6 October 2026

Added

  • Report a bug / Send feedback (#82): press Alt+Shift+F, or click "Report" in the drawer, popup or Settings, or "Report a bug" in the dashboard. Write one line, choose Bug or Idea, and press Enter. BenchPilot adds the page (no query string), screen, version and plan; it never adds your leads, contacts or consultants. An optional screenshot is off by default (on for the founder's admin account). Reports that can't be sent are saved and retried. They go to BenchPilot's server in Mumbai and are deleted after 12 months.
  • Grievance Officer in the privacy policy (India DPDP Act): acknowledgement within 7 days, resolution within 30 days.
  • Backup & Restore, free on every plan (#77): Settings → Data → "Download full backup" saves one file with all leads, vendors, consultants, notes, jobs, templates, profile, settings and résumé files. "Restore from backup" checks the file, shows what's in it, saves a safety copy of your current data first, then replaces everything. Your account, plan and monthly reveal count are never in the file and are never restored. Settings shows "Last backup", and the dashboard shows a reminder after 7 days without one.

Changed

  • No desktop notifications (#80): BenchPilot never pops up on your desktop any more.
  • "Match bench" counts posts (#76): one post that fits three consultants counts once, not three times.
  • Pro list (#77): "JSON backup export" is now "JSON export of leads"; full backup is free for everyone.

Removed

  • Desktop notifications, quiet hours and the night digest (#80), and the notifications permission. Old alert settings and alarms are cleaned up on update.
  • Auto-Scroller (#77). It scrolled LinkedIn on its own, which LinkedIn can treat as automation and restrict accounts for, and it broke our rule that BenchPilot never scrolls or clicks for you. Removed from the popup, Settings, the Pro plan and the upgrade page. Its old settings are cleaned up on update.

Fixed

  • Fake emails (#75): ordinary sentences were read as emails ("Java developer at google.com" became developer@google.com; "2:30 pm EST at abc.com" became est@abc.com). Only real addresses are captured now, including "name [at] company [dot] com" and "john.smith at abc dot com". An address glued to the next word ("x@abc.comPhone") is cut correctly.
  • Wrong recruiter from comments (#75): an email in a comment or a chat window could be saved as the post's recruiter. Only emails in the post itself (or its author header) count.
  • Lost requirements (#75): when one recruiter posted several requirements, only the first was kept. Each post now gets its own card, and a post seen again fills in a missing role, location or posted time.
  • Wrong person on re-shared requirements (#69): the poster's name, profile and phone were saved on someone else's email. New Cleanup check "Name doesn't match email" repairs older leads.
  • Misleading match % (#76):

Added

Updates live while you scroll LinkedIn.

Free: 3 alerts a day; Basic and Pro: unlimited; quiet hours and the digest are Pro. Never for imports. Posts older than 48 hours don't alert.

Version 1.5.2 5 October 2026

Fixed

  • Bench matching (#54): a consultant could "match" hundreds of requirements (one shared skill was enough), including full-time jobs. Matching is now a 0–100 % score (skills 45, title 20, location 15, experience 10, visa and engagement 10) with a "Why" line, and only matches of 60 % or more are shown. Never matched: hotlists, bench sellers, recruiter job openings, full-time / W2-only / "no C2C" posts, local-only posts in another state (unless the consultant relocates) and visa conflicts ("GC/USC only", "No H1B", "Independent visa only"). One shared skill is not a match; common words like AI, SQL, Data count for less.
  • Lead name (#53): a section heading in the post ("Ideal Candidate Profile") could become the lead's name. The post author's name now wins; a name from the signature is used only when there is none, or when the post comes from a company page.
  • Local only (#53): a Location line ending in "Locals" ("Chicago, IL (Hybrid) Locals"), "(Locals)", "looking for locals" and "local candidates / profiles" are tagged Local only.
  • Notes (#53): "Experience" with no value no longer shows as a cut-off "erience".

Added

  • Word résumés (#55): consultants and My profile accept .docx as well as PDF (up to 5 MB). Text is read on your computer by a built-in reader (no outside code) and fills the same suggestions. View downloads a Word file. Old .doc files show "Please save it as .docx or PDF".

Version 1.5.1 2 October 2026

Fixed

  • "Bench Sales" is no longer a default target designation (bench sales people are sellers, not leads).

Added

  • Mark as bench seller (drawer menu and dashboard lead panel): marks the person and labels their company Bench seller (not hiring), so future posts from that company are flagged. Never overwrites another company label without saying so.
  • Cleanup → Possible bench sellers: finds saved leads that look like bench sellers (hotlist posts, bench sales headlines, four or more unrelated role families) for one-click or bulk review. Free on every plan.
  • Leads view: post type filter (Requirement / Hotlist / Unclear / Bench seller) and a Bench seller chip. Import suggests the Bench seller label for tabs named "bench", "hotlist" or "seller". Pitching a bench seller shows a reminder.
  • Jobs for you (#45): LinkedIn posts where a company hires a recruiter for itself are job openings for you, not consultant requirements. A new dashboard view keeps them apart: title, company, location and work mode, contact, status (New, Applied, Interview, Offer, Rejected, Closed), notes that save when you click away, Open post and Delete. Apply opens an email draft (your chosen email app) to the poster, written from the new My profile in Settings (name, title, email, phone, LinkedIn, summary and a résumé PDF), and marks the job Applied. Profile, résumé and jobs stay on your computer. New worker messages SAVE_JOB, UPDATE_JOB, DELETE_JOB, GET_JOBS, SAVE_MY_PROFILE.
  • Requirement tags in Leads: Local (area), Remote / Hybrid / Onsite and engagement chips show on each lead and in the lead panel, with new filters for Local only, work mode and engagement. A lead that is really a job opening shows Move to Jobs for you.
  • Local-only requirements and tags (#44): the classifier also reads local-only phrases ("local candidates only", "must be local to …"), work mode (Remote / Hybrid / Onsite, with negations) and engagement (C2C, W2, 1099, contract, full-time, C2H). Requirement cards show Local: <area> and the other tags; new Local only filter; Remote / C2C / W2 filters use the tags. For local-only posts, Matches my bench only suggests consultants in that state or willing to relocate.
  • Jobs for you in the drawer (#44): posts where a company hires a US IT / bench sales / technical recruiter (or talent acquisition, account manager, BDM for staffing) for itself are classified as job openings. They are never leads (no reveal, no autosave, no Pitch) and appear under a Jobs for you chip with Save job and Apply (email draft from My profile; you attach your résumé and send).

Version 1.5.0 1 October 2026

Added

  • Vendors view: recruiters grouped into companies by email domain (Gmail and similar never grouped), with labels (Trusted, Avoid, Direct client, Prime vendor, Implementation partner), notes, recruiter counts and last activity. Rename, merge (with domain aliases for future leads) and move recruiters between companies. Label chip and filter in the Leads view.
  • Avoid / Trusted badges in the LinkedIn drawer and on the profile card, including for recruiters not saved yet.
  • Excel and CSV import (free on every plan): built-in .xlsx reader (no third-party code), a label per workbook tab, automatic column mapping with manual override, preview (new, already saved, skipped with a download, duplicates), existing data kept by default, and Undo import until the next import.
  • Database cleanup: possible duplicates (same person at a company, mistyped email copies, same LinkedIn profile, same phone), missing-data filters, and bounced emails marked by the user. Merge (with Undo), "not duplicates" and clearing bounced emails need Basic or Pro.
  • Résumé PDF on consultants: upload (PDF up to 5 MB), view, download, replace and remove. Files stay in the extension's own database on the user's computer (new unlimitedStorage permission). Text is read with bundled pdf.js 5.7.284 and shown as suggestions to review before anything is applied. Pro keeps version history.
  • Consultant Email and Phone fields, filled from résumé suggestions.
  • Pitch messages for each consultant: LinkedIn connection note (200 characters or fewer), short direct message and hotlist line, personalised for the recruiter when known. Copy only; nothing is sent automatically.
  • Quick notes: saved message snippets with Copy, or Insert into the LinkedIn message box the user clicked (never sends). Free 3, Basic 20, Pro unlimited.
  • Rate calculator: W2 / 1099 / C2C gross margin per hour, percentage and month, and the highest pay rate for a target margin.

Changed

  • Upgrade page lists quick notes, cleanup and résumé history per plan.
